title: 1989 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Let \(n\) be a positive integer. If the equation \(2x+2y+z=n\) has \(28\) solutions in positive integers \(x,\) \(y\) and \(z,\) then \(n\) must be either

solutions.text:
For \(s=x+y\ge2,\) there are \(s-1\) positive ordered pairs \((x,y),\) and \(z=n-2s\) is positive when \(s\le\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor.\) Writing \(m=\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor,\) the number of solutions is \[ \sum_{s=2}^{m}(s-1)=\frac{m(m-1)}2. \] Setting this equal to \(28\) gives \(m=8.\) Hence \(\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor=8,\) so \(n=17\) or \(18.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: For fixed \(s,\) count the positive ordered pairs \((x,y)\) and require \(n-2s\ge1\)
